verdict.rationale: Floot's platform docs say apps built on it get scheduled jobs that run without a server to keep alive. That is a first-party recurring background-automation capability, not a one-off action, but it rests on a single thin line. Missing for 10: documentation of how to create and configure scheduled jobs or triggers, event-driven (non-schedule) automations, monitoring or run history for background jobs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Jobs that run on a schedule, without a server to keep alive.
